subject: DPA questions — transient sandbox snapshots, escrow copies, and deletion verification

From: Sara Liao <sara.liao@acmeco.com>

Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@acmeco.com>
Date: 2027-12-05T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on sandbox snapshot retention + DPA redline

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our legal and security teams are reviewing the DPA redline and had a few targeted questions before we proceed to countersign. I've attached our current redline (Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.docx). High level asks: 

1) Sandbox snapshots / ephemeral copies — the redline currently says "Customer data will be deleted within X days of termination" without distinguishing environment. For our security posture we need clarity: can you confirm whether snapshots taken of sandbox/test environments (containing production-like subsets) are subject to the same erase window, or do you offer a shorter transient retention (e.g., 7–30 days) for sandbox only?

2) Escrow / third-party backups — we have an internal control that escrowed snapshots (for disaster recovery / escrow purposes) must be kept onshore and require explicit retention periods. Does Redwood maintain any third-party escrow copies by default? If so, how does that interact with the erase obligations?

3) Proof of deletion — our auditors often require a deletion manifest showing which copies were removed and where (including any offsite backups) and the date/time. What level of evidence can Redwood provide on request?

4) Debugging exceptions — we sometimes request short, one-off exceptions where a snapshot is retained slightly longer for a production incident post-termination. Is there a documented process for exception approvals?

If you can provide short answers and (ideally) a proposed redline snippet we can review, that would speed things up. We'd like to avoid an open-ended clause that could legalize lengthy retention in non-prod.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 30-min call if easier.

Sara
Sara Liao
Senior Security Manager, AcmeCloud

Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kim (legal) and Jonas (ops) to confirm details and draft a short redline snippet we can propose back.

High level from product/ops perspective: Redwood treats "sandbox" and "production" snapshots differently operationally — sandbox snapshots are not journaled into long-term backups by default, and we can commit to a shorter, bounded erase window for sandbox environments. That said, there are edge cases (customer-requested exports, escrow, or legally compelled holds) that can change the flow. Kim/Jonas — can you confirm the conservative suggested language for the DPA and what proof we can commit to?

Would you like us to propose a 30-day transient window for sandbox by default, with an explicit carveout for documented exceptions (escrow requests, legal holds), or would Acme prefer 7/14/30 as the default?

If agreeable, I'll draft something and send a brief note for countersign.

Ben / Jonas —

Below are recommended positions and a short redline snippet we can propose to Acme. I've kept the language operationally feasible and defensible for audits. Key constraints we should flag to the customer:

- Production data: maintain current clause — erase within 90 days of termination (covers deletion, backup rotation, and propagation across replicas).
- Sandbox / transient environments: propose a separate clause. Suggested default: "Transient sandbox snapshots that are not promoted to production will be deleted within thirty (30) days of creation or within thirty (30) days of Customer termination, whichever occurs first." That prevents indefinite retention but gives a predictable window.
- Escrow / DR copies: Redwood does not maintain escrow copies by default for hosted customers. If Customer requires escrowed snapshots or vendor-managed offsite archival for DR, we propose that: (a) such copies are retained only by express written agreement and (b) retention periods for escrowed copies will be capped (e.g., 180 days) and subject to onshore requirements where agreed.
- Proof of deletion: we can provide a deletion evidence package consisting of (i) snapshot IDs removed, (ii) timestamped deletion logs from the storage layer, and (iii) a signed statement from Redwood operations. We cannot provide immutable guarantees across third-party escrow providers unless Redwood is the escrow custodian. For customer-requested exports or S3 exports, the customer controls the copy.
- Debugging / incident exceptions: recommend an "exception approval" flow — customer submits a written request to security@redwood.example.com; exceptions are timeboxed (max 90 days) and must include purpose and approver. We can commit to logging and an approval manifest.

Proposed redline snippet (copy/paste friendly):

"For clarity, 'Transient Sandbox Snapshots' means any snapshot of Customer data created in non-production environments (including but not limited to dev, test, and staging) that is not promoted to production. Redwood will delete Transient Sandbox Snapshots within thirty (30) days of creation or within thirty (30) days following termination of Customer's account, whichever occurs earlier. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may request an exception for incident investigation or regulatory need by written request; exceptions must be approved in writing and will be time-limited as documented in Redwood's exception approval playbook.

Redwood does not create or retain third-party escrow copies by default. Escrow or third-party archival copies (if requested by Customer) will be governed by a separate written agreement which will include explicit retention limits (no more than one hundred eighty (180) days unless otherwise agreed) and control-plane logging.

Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide evidence of deletion (snapshot IDs, storage-layer deletion timestamps, and operator-signed deletion confirmation) within thirty (30) days of request, subject to reasonable verification steps."

Attachments: redline_snippet.txt (plain text, 2KB)

Jonas — can ops confirm that we can produce the storage-layer deletion timestamps and operator-signed confirmation within 30 days? If yes, I'll send to Sara with the snippet and a proposed DocuSign link for their countersign.

-Kim
